title: MIT News
description: Official MIT News: research, campus, and latest articles.

items.title: Professor Emeritus Chiang Chung Mei, pioneering scholar of ocean wave dynamics and fluid mechanics, dies at 91
items.content_text: A towering figure in theoretical hydrodynamics is remembered for his intellectual rigor, generosity, and lifelong devotion to his students.

items.title: Drug that targets an inflammatory enzyme could help prevent lung cancer
items.content_text: A new study by MIT researchers shows that inhibiting caspase-1 can reduce the risk of tumor growth.

items.title: Cells pulse together as they grow — and malignant cells pulse the longest
items.content_text: MIT researchers discovered a cellular dance that may offer clues to the development of cancer, asthma, and other diseases.

items.title: High-speed microscopy reveals electrical activity across the brain
items.content_text: The new technique could help scientists learn how the entire brain works to generate decisions and emotions.

items.title: Researchers uncover hidden pore network within nuclear fuel
items.content_text: New understanding of how nuclear fuel breaks down and changes in an operating nuclear reactor could help keep some reactors running longer, will inform the next generation of nuclear reactor fuel systems.

items.title: Featured video: An “MIT story” about an iconic professor
items.content_text: A new short film from MIT Open Learning explores the influential career of Institute Professor and School of Engineering Dean Paula Hammond.

items.title: MIT selected to lead new NSF materials research center
items.content_text: The Materials Research Science and Engineering Center unites researchers across disciplines to develop technologies for medical imaging, sustainable metals production, and next-generation electronics.

items.title: Astronomers discover a brand-new type of astrophysical object: A black hole star
items.content_text: The mashup of a black hole and an enormous star has never been seen before and could explain the mysterious little red dots often found in deep-space images.

items.title: Met Warehouse opens as the new home of MIT’s School of Architecture and Planning
items.content_text: In a feat of adaptive reuse, a massive, century-old brick storage facility has been turned into a contemporary hub for collaboration and creative work.

items.title: How to design a space habitat that supports its residents’ mental health
items.content_text: A new online platform helps engineers look beyond survival mode when designing habitats for extreme living conditions.

items.title: 3 Questions: MIT Sloan launches Evening MBA
items.content_text: Dean Richard Locke discusses a new program that expands access for working professionals while deepening connections to Greater Boston’s innovation economy.

items.title: The mystery of the Chinese tea chest label
items.content_text: MIT historian Tristan Brown uncovers the true origins of an artifact once thought to be a relic of the Boston Tea Party.

items.title: On the hunt for dark matter
items.content_text: From Broadway to MIT’s Laboratory for Nuclear Science, PhD student Jessica Fry doesn’t do anything halfway. Now she’s hunting for the universe’s most elusive particle.

items.title: With a feel for physics, AI models simulate a wider range of real-world scenarios
items.content_text: “GeoPT” helps AI models understand the basics of physics so they can simulate how objects respond to things like wind and water more efficiently and accurately.

items.title: High-orbit satellites could light the way for travel to the moon
items.content_text: Acting as cooperative optical beacons, the satellites could provide GPS-like navigation and communications support for spacecraft operating across cislunar space.

items.title: MIT researchers tackle the economic realities of fusion power
items.content_text: Their new study aims to give budding industry a framework for understanding how fusion can be profitable.

items.title: Physicists watch a material’s electrons assemble, and reassemble, into coexisting phases
items.content_text: The study could help scientists understand how superconductivity and other more complex phenomena emerge in quantum materials.

items.title: Akirah Bradley-Armstrong named vice chancellor for student life
items.content_text: An experienced student affairs leader is joining MIT to oversee the next chapter for the Division of Student Life.

items.title: A new way to watch heat move through electronics
items.content_text: MIT researchers can now precisely measure how heat moves through multilayered materials like computer chips.

items.title: Then and now: How MIT Lincoln Laboratory has served as a driving force in national security innovation
items.content_text: Members of the laboratory community reflect on technology impacts that shaped the United States and the world over the past 75 years.

items.title: Scientists unveil more than 600 new tissue models of human cancer
items.content_text: Derived from patient tumor samples and available to researchers around the world, the cells will aid the development of new cancer treatments.

items.title: Researchers make air-stable, ultrathin superconductors, for more scalable quantum devices
items.content_text: A new technique produces wafer-scale samples, overcoming a major roadblock to using these materials in quantum technologies.

items.title: These 3D-printed objects can tell you if they’re being used properly
items.content_text: The “ShiftLens” design and fabrication system creates objects that change their surface appearance based on user interactions, without any electronics.

items.title: Past is prologue for geopolitical developments
items.content_text: DUSP Associate Professor Jason Jackson’s latest book compares how two countries chose radically different paths to economic independence.

items.title: Reframing leadership as a design problem
items.content_text: Nicholas de Monchaux reflects on guiding the MIT Department of Architecture through a period of dramatic change for the profession.

items.title: Solving the solvent problem
items.content_text: By focusing on electrolytes, MIT scientists are making sodium-metal batteries a more practical energy storage option.

items.title: The benefits of medical AI assistance vary based on user expertise
items.content_text: Study finds non-experts deferred to LLM-based diagnostic assistance, even when it was wrong, while clinicians caught AI errors.

items.title: Alexander Rakhlin named director of  the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center
items.content_text: An expert in machine learning, statistics, and computation, Rakhlin succeeds Professor Ankur Moitra.

items.title: Connecting students with the future of microelectronics
items.content_text: The 2026 NEMC Hub-sponsored externship gave students access to world-class research, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, and professionals driving innovation across the Northeast.

items.title: Turning molecules into reliable electronic devices
items.content_text: A new fabrication platform integrates molecules into electronic devices, opening the door to emerging computing technologies.

items.title: Using reason, again and again
items.content_text: Philosopher Brian Hedden studies decision-making over time — and recently chose to return to alma mater MIT, where he is now connecting ethics and computing.

items.title: Building energy security through more sustainable batteries
items.content_text: PhD student Hugh Smith works to develop sodium-ion batteries, whose components are more abundant and accessible than those of conventional lithium-ion technology.

items.title: Daniela Rus receives Bavarian Minister-President's High-Tech Prize
items.content_text: Director of CSAIL and MIT professor honored for her contributions to robotics, artificial intelligence, and autonomous systems.

items.title: Connecting research to policy on Capitol Hill
items.content_text: MIT students and postdocs discussed science funding and research with policymakers in Washington during the MIT Science Policy Initiative’s annual Congressional Visit Days.

items.title: Why some nitrogen-processing enzymes are more efficient than others
items.content_text: New findings could help researchers design synthetic catalysts that convert nitrogen gas to ammonia, a key step in fertilizer production.

items.title: MIT and Broad Institute researchers break diffraction barrier in super-resolution microscopy
items.content_text: New U-STORM imaging technology lets scientists view molecular structures in subatomic detail — about 1,000 times clearer than traditional dyes — while making the microscope process much simpler.

items.title: How a medical database developed at MIT evolved into a global standard of data-sharing
items.content_text: The visionary PhysioNet platform launched 25 years ago, based on a system developed at MIT in the 1970s. It has become one of the most comprehensive biomedical and clinical data repositories in existence.

items.title: Professor Emeritus Robert Cohen, pioneering polymers researcher and devoted mentor, dies at 79
items.content_text: Architect of MIT’s interdisciplinary Program in Polymers and Soft Matter and the PhD in chemical engineering practice is remembered for his passion for mentorship and education.

items.title: Yu Deng ’11 and Hong Wang PhD ’19 awarded Fields Medal
items.content_text: MIT-trained mathematicians earn the honor, one of the most prestigious in the field, for their significant achievements.

items.title: Making robots faster by helping them think ahead
items.content_text: By planning actions based on the future position of a robot, the VLASH technique streamlines motions and accelerates performance.

items.title: MIT engineers design recyclable elastic yarn
items.content_text: Melt it, spin it, use it again. This new recyclable yarn is as strong and stretchy as spandex-based yarns.

items.title: Looking beyond research
items.content_text: Professor Anna-Christina Eilers is “Committed to Caring” for building a culture around attentiveness and community.

items.title: MIT projects selected for funding under US Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission
items.content_text: Initial research projects advance national priorities across natural resources, manufacturing, nuclear physics, and more.

items.title: MIT student leaders: Q&A with men’s soccer captain Dilin Meloni
items.content_text: The rising senior is passionate about soccer, nuclear fusion, and advocating on behalf of his fellow student-athletes at MIT.

items.title: Professor Emeritus Dimitri Bertsekas, influential computer scientist and prolific author, dies at 83
items.content_text: Known for his clear and elegant writing style, Bertsekas shaped fields from control and optimization to large-scale computation and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Diffuse puffs of “missing” matter surround most galaxies
items.content_text: An MIT-led team used bright radio bursts to illuminate a vast source of matter that was previously unaccounted for.

items.title: Engineering Design Studio hosts alumni on their fifth, 10th … and 55th reunions
items.content_text: A recent reunion activity, taught by EECS Senior Lecturer Gim Hom, doubled as both his “last class” and a chance to reconnect with classmates.

items.title: MIT honors employees with 2026 Excellence Awards, Collier Medal, and Staff Award for Distinction in Service
items.content_text: The MIT community celebrated the talent, dedication, and impact of its staff.

items.title: Emery Brown, Daniel Hastings, and Douglas Lauffenburger named Institute Professors
items.content_text: Longtime professors and experts in the fields of anesthesiology, aerospace engineering, and biological engineering, respectively, receive MIT’s highest faculty honor.

items.title: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences welcomes six new faculty for 2026
items.content_text: New professors join the Comparative Media Studies/Writing, Economics, Linguistics, and Music and Theater Arts departments.

items.title: Following the questions where they lead
items.content_text: Assistant Professor Bailey Flanigan has arrived at complex computational methods for helping democracy thrive.

items.title: How an influx of salt may affect microbial ecosystems
items.content_text: As sea levels rise and saltwater seeps into freshwater, stressed aquatic populations may retain overall growth even as diversity declines, MIT scientists find.

items.title: Diana Grass: Listening to the body’s language
items.content_text: The PhD candidate builds soft bioelectronic technologies to decode signals between the brain and the rest of the body.

items.title: For energy systems that power a reliable grid, the future is all about location
items.content_text: MIT researchers find that where new energy projects are built could be key to avoiding blackouts in a future with hotter weather and other challenges.

items.title: A better way to turn 2D designs into 3D models for rapid prototyping
items.content_text: Researchers developed an automated framework that helps AI models generate CAD programs more accurately and efficiently.

items.title: 3 Questions: Neural transparency and the future of AI design
items.content_text: Assistant Professor Pat Pataranutaporn describes a new interface that lets everyday users glimpse inside an AI's neural network before their chatbot ever says a word.

items.title: MIT Professor Susumu Tonegawa, renowned molecular biologist and Nobel laureate, dies at 86
items.content_text: Tonegawa made landmark discoveries about how the immune system generates antibody diversity and how the brain forms memories.

items.title: 3D-printed bridge points the way to greener construction
items.content_text: MIT researchers developed a framework that folds a printer’s real-world limits into the optimization, while revealing that better hardware could sharply reduce material use.

items.title: Electric fields help guide neural activity, even from moment to moment
items.content_text: A new study adds evidence that electric fields in the brain help to organize and shape underlying neural activity via “ephaptic coupling.”

items.title: Ketogenic diets may increase cancer risk in the small intestine
items.content_text: MIT researchers have found that a ketogenic high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet fuels the growth of intestinal tumors.

items.title: Helping AI models to meet the real world
items.content_text: Through research and entrepreneurship, Professor Devavrat Shah is helping to design methods that can handle constant decision-making using limited computational resources.

items.title: Three MIT Press journals lead their fields with Clarivate No. 1 rankings
items.content_text: Computational Linguistics, International Security, and The Review of Economics and Statistics lead their disciplines with 2026 Clarivate impact factors.

items.title: How visual learning happens in the brain
items.content_text: Scientists find that learning to identify a new object subtly reshapes visual processing in the brain.

items.title: Can AI build a jet engine? JARVIS Challenge tests role of AI copilots in tough-tech engineering
items.content_text: MIT students designed, built, and tested a jet engine with AI copilots, assessing AI’s usefulness in developing high-performance aerospace systems.

items.title: MIT engineers find a precise way to grow artificial blood vessels
items.content_text: Gently stretching and pulling a “blood vessel on a chip” encourages controlled sprouting of new vessels, for possible use in artificial tissues or organs.

items.title: Arthur Bahr named head of MIT’s Literature Section
items.content_text: A faculty member since 2007, the scholar of medieval literature explores how different parts of physical manuscripts combine to create interest and meaning.

items.title: How MIT students are helping to prevent cyberattacks
items.content_text: Students from the MIT Cybersecurity Clinic help local governments and other vulnerable organizations defend against digital threats.

items.title: AI agents create virtual playgrounds to help robots get crucial training data
items.content_text: “SceneSmith” system uses collaborative AI agents to create realistic 3D environments of places like kitchens, hotels, and living rooms, where robots can simulate everyday chores.

items.title: Tiny infrared chip could improve detection of gases and heat
items.content_text: The tunable device controls mid-infrared light for more precise thermal imaging, chemical sensing, or pollution monitoring.

items.title: New method aims to keep kids safe from illegal AI-generated content
items.content_text: Researchers developed an auditing technique to test generative AI models for malicious capabilities, without prompting them for illegal outputs.

items.title: Discovery could lead to brighter, more energy-efficient digital displays
items.content_text: Researchers found a simple solution for extending the lifespans of LEDs made from glowing microscopic particles called quantum dots.

items.title: MIT-led project opens first climate shelter in Bangladesh
items.content_text: The Jameel Observatory-CREWSnet project opens a solar-powered “adaptation fortress” in Satkhira, a region facing severe and growing climate threats.

items.title: New flapping robot swims and flies like a diving bird
items.content_text: MIT engineers’ design could lead to a new class of aerial-aquatic vehicles for ocean exploration.

items.title: Beyond the pitch: The founder’s journey
items.content_text: An MIT mechanical engineering course explores entrepreneurship through lessons and stories shared by alumni startup founders.

items.title: A baseball-sized sensor can detect chemical threats
items.content_text: The “TOSSIT” device, developed at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, can warn service members and first responders of dangerous vapors and aerosols.

items.title: Tiny robot boats build floating structures
items.content_text: MIT researchers developed FloatForm, a swarm of small aquatic robots that snap together like ants forming a raft, assembling into reconfigurable structures on the water.

items.title: Bringing the data to every sideline
items.content_text: PhD candidate Henry Wang works with FIFA and other organizations to advance the way sports are played, analyzed, and refereed.

items.title: Ana Miljački named head of the Department of Architecture
items.content_text: In this leadership role, Miljački seeks to shepherd a collective commitment to transform the present into a better future.

items.title: Separating logic and language
items.content_text: Neuroscientists find logical reasoning does not involve language-processing parts of the brain.

items.title: MIT-designed educational factory embraces modern manufacturing
items.content_text: MIT and Tec de Monterrey will expand FrED curriculum to universities across Mexico.

items.title: MIT researcher proposes a way to detect nuclear weapons in space
items.content_text: The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans nuclear weapons in space, but there’s currently no way to verify that satellites aren’t carrying them.

items.title: MIT engineers whip up a more breathable hydrogel
items.content_text: The new aerated material could enable longer-lasting bandages, implants, and wearable sensors.

items.title: The brain’s internal ruler
items.content_text: A simple brain circuit measures objects’ distance from the body using touch signals from a rodent’s whiskers, MIT scientists find.

items.title: How novice coders can develop AI programs for military applications
items.content_text: A USAF cadet and a Lincoln Laboratory researcher found AI chatbots can help nontechnical service members produce viable software applications for their unique problems.

items.title: Many black holes had past lives, new research shows
items.content_text: Physicists have found signs of colliding black holes that are themselves products of previous black hole smash-ups.

items.title: Hydrogen: clean fuel of the future — if we can find a cheap and clean way to ship it
items.content_text: A team led by MIT Energy Initiative researchers developed the HyCAT tool, enabling decision-makers to explore the cost and carbon emissions of their options for shipping hydrogen fuel to their site.

items.title: Jesse Thaler named director of the Laboratory for Nuclear Science
items.content_text: The professor of physics and inaugural director of the NSF AI Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions will lead LNS and continue his research in particle physics.

items.title: Toward a future that preserves benefits of neurotechnology for all
items.content_text: PhD student Rachel Sava, winner of the Envisioning the Future of Computing Prize, explores transformative improvements and dystopian risks of neural technology.

items.title: Discovery helps explain why solid-state batteries often fail
items.content_text: New research could help prevent the formation of tiny seeds of lithium metal within the electrolyte, enabling batteries that charge faster and last longer.

items.title: Lerna Ekmekcioglu named head of MIT’s History Section
items.content_text: A faculty member since 2011, Ekmekcioglu examines how communities survive, adapt, remember, and make claims on justice under difficult political conditions.

items.title: Why are some bacterial genes high in purines?
items.content_text: In certain species of bacteria, the answer lies in shielding RNA transcripts from a quality-control factor called Rho. Understanding the requirements for expressible sequences is critical for expression engineering of therapeutic agents.

items.title: Building a scholarly community
items.content_text: The SHASS Faculty Fellows Program, administered by the MIT Human Insight Collaborative, is fostering new research projects and creating space for supportive and interdisciplinary discussion.

items.title: MIT in the media: Innovating and educating for the next 250 years of America
items.content_text: During a "Washington Post Live" panel discussion with ASU President Michael Crow, President Sally Kornbluth explored how universities are preparing the next generation of scientists to lead in America’s rapidly changing technological landscape.

items.title: Boleslaw Wyslouch steps down as director of Laboratory for Nuclear Science
items.content_text: Wyslouch remains the director of the Bates Research and Engineering Center and will continue research on heavy ion collisions.

items.title: How urban design leads to better wellness
items.content_text: An extensive study of U.S. cities identifies walkable neighborhoods, urban greenery, and access to amenities as key contributors to residents’ health.

items.title: A portable ultrasound system could make reliable breast imaging more accessible
items.content_text: The new technology, which generates high-resolution, 3D images of breast tissue, requires no expertise to operate and could be used at home.

items.title: MIT-Kalaniyot program expands, with new cohort of scholars
items.content_text: The innovative effort bringing researchers from Israel to campus keeps growing while enhancing community connections and academic inquiry.

items.title: The brain’s language network is more extensive than previously thought
items.content_text: A new study reveals that parts of the brain located far from the canonical language-processing centers are also involved in language comprehension.

items.title: MIT student teams win top honors in NASA competition
items.content_text: Three MIT teams took five top awards in the 2026 NASA RASC-AL Competition for designing critical elements for the moon base and future missions to Mars.

items.title: MIT researchers advance toward greater bandwidth, more energy-efficient communications
items.content_text: The FUTUR-IC research program integrates electronics and photonics in microchip systems.

items.title: Q&A: What is agentic AI today, and what do we want it to be?
items.content_text: Computer scientist Phillip Isola cuts through the hype to explain how AI agents work and what the future might hold for this rapidly advancing technology.

items.title: Two MIT faculty members named 2026 Pew Biomedical Scholars
items.content_text: Cell biologist Whitney Henry and immunologist Harikesh Wong will receive four years of flexible funding to advance early-career research on ferroptosis and immune decision-making.

items.title: Inaugural Music Technology Research Showcase celebrates work of new graduate program’s initial students
items.content_text: Associate Professor Anna Huang delivers the keynote address, “In Search of Human-AI Resonance,” to a capacity crowd.

items.title: Scientists find ozone depletion began decades before discovery of ozone hole
items.content_text: Using modern tools, they also determined that carbon tetrachloride, used as a dry-cleaning and degreasing agent as early as the 1930s, was at the root of early ozone loss.

items.title: 3 Questions: Beyond data-driven aesthetics
items.content_text: In a new Keller Gallery exhibition, Alexandros Haridis SM ’17, PhD ’22 traces centuries of ideas about aesthetic judgment and explores how design can make complex computational systems visible.

items.title: Care in the midst of pressure
items.content_text: Anantha P. Chandrakasan is “Committed to Caring” for redefining mentorship through presence and perspective.

items.title: Graphene can hold multiple states of superconductivity, a new study finds
items.content_text: What’s more, the superconducting states get stronger under conditions expected to kill them.

items.title: David Autor named head of the Department of Economics
items.content_text: A faculty member since 1999, Autor is a leading researcher in artificial intelligence and the work of the future.

items.title: Antenna array could provide protected tactical satellite communications in low-Earth orbit
items.content_text: The prototype array uses a small, lightweight, low-power, and low-cost aperture.

items.title: How data centers can better manage energy use
items.content_text: A new study suggests flexibility in the timing of electricity consumption could lower consumer costs.

items.title: Students from across the Northeast step inside MIT.nano’s cleanroom
items.content_text: A hands-on boot camp teaches integrated photonics to community and four-year college students in the region.

items.title: MIT in the media: Exploring how curiosity-driven science is an essential ingredient in America’s success
items.content_text: “Scientific American” showcases the history and future of America’s scientific engine, highlighting promising young scientists and icons at MIT and beyond.

items.title: Improving the speed and energy-efficiency of AI agents
items.content_text: A new system, known as Murakkab, optimizes the design and deployment of multistep workflows that power AI applications.

items.title: How architecture influences political activity
items.content_text: In Ghana, semi-communal “compound houses” affect how much people vote and participate in political activity, new research shows.

items.title: What happens when environmental change outpaces life’s ability to adapt?
items.content_text: A new model links Earth’s mass extinctions to mismatches between rates of environmental change and biological adaptation.

items.title: Computer model could enable bridges and buildings that use less material
items.content_text: MIT researchers developed an approach for generating more buildable structures, bridging the gap between optimized design and real-world construction.

items.title: New chip could help tiny robots traverse complex environments
items.content_text: Researchers combined an efficient algorithm with dedicated hardware to rapidly generate 3D maps for navigation using minimal memory and power.

items.title: A better way to model the behavior of metal alloys
items.content_text: MIT researchers’ approach captures subtle atomic patterns, improving predictions of material properties.

items.title: MIT in the media: For the future of tech, "Massachusetts can absolutely lead"
items.content_text: Leaders, faculty across MIT discuss fostering innovation and talent in Greater Boston in special series of articles published alongside the outlet's annual list of 'Tech Power Players'

items.title: Susan Solomon named 2026 Tang Prize laureate
items.content_text: The MIT professor’s groundbreaking work on atmospheric chemistry helped lay steps towards recovery of the ozone layer and demonstrated the lasting impacts of carbon emissions on Earth’s climate.

items.title: Could AI tell you where you left your keys?
items.content_text: A new spatial memory system for robots efficiently captures details about the objects they see while exploring their environment.

items.title: How to create distinguishable states for quantum systems
items.content_text: Researchers establish key insights for reading and writing information for quantum sensing, communication, computing, and control.

items.title: Pablo Jarillo-Herrero wins Kavli Prize in Nanoscience
items.content_text: The MIT physicist shares the honor with two others for foundational research establishing the field of twistronics.
